notable_observations: 278 Node DEP0169 url.parse() deprecation/security warnings across many API routes

current_argus_context.interpretation: These observations prioritize Control Plane failure truth and failure memory. They do not establish model-quality failure.

execute_next.action: Add a shadow/work-branch Control Plane failure ledger and reason taxonomy that records every cron/provider/storage/auth failure with request or run identity, persistence state, severity, recurrence count and recovery state before any further model-complexity work.
execute_next.why_now: Current production telemetry contains storage/auth failures and a broad recurring runtime warning, while Vercel provides requestId/invocationId/traceId and API-Football exposes authoritative quota headers. ARGUS needs one auditable truth surface so infrastructure failures cannot be mistaken for prediction failures or silently forgotten.
execute_next.expected_benefit: Faster root-cause isolation, fewer silent failures, explicit recurrence memory, safer cron learning, clearer operator UX, and better protection against corrupted or incomplete evidence.
execute_next.evidence_level: HIGH for observability primitives; MEDIUM for the exact ARGUS taxonomy until exercised prospectively.
execute_next.minimum_test: Instrument one non-critical research cron plus read-only aggregation of existing runtime failures for 7 days; make no model, threshold, polling-frequency or production-state changes.
success_metrics: 100% of observed 5xx and cron execution failures receive a non-UNKNOWN reason code
100% of instrumented cron runs have CONFIGURED->DEPLOYED->INVOKED->SUCCEEDED/FAILED->PERSISTED/NOT_PERSISTED lineage
recurrences link to the same failure family rather than creating isolated anonymous events
instrumentation adds zero provider calls and no measurable decision mutation
execute_next.failure_condition: Instrumentation changes runtime behavior materially, loses run identity, produces ambiguous reason codes on repeated failures, creates duplicate writes, or increases provider consumption.
execute_next.proof_required: Seven-day prospective ledger with sampled request/log cross-checks, persistence acknowledgements, duplicate detection and zero unexplained gaps.
execute_next.rollback: Disable the research ledger writer/aggregator and retain existing Watchtower/runtime logs; no model or prediction state is changed.

source: Vercel structured application logging guidance, updated 2026-05-28
findings.evidence: Vercel exposes requestId, traceId, invocationId, route, environment, deployment and status metadata; structured application logs are recommended for application-specific error IDs and causal fields. ARGUS currently has recurring and isolated runtime failures that are not yet centralized into durable failure memory.
findings.why_it_matters: A forecasting system cannot be professionally audited if data/model failures and infrastructure failures share the same vague unhealthy state or disappear after logs expire.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Create a read-only failure aggregator plus append-only research ledger for one non-critical cron and existing 5xx events.
findings.required_evidence: 7 prospective days, 100% reason classification for instrumented failures, sampled one-to-one correlation with Vercel request/run identifiers.
findings.failure_condition: Unknown reasons remain common, duplicate records proliferate, or instrumentation changes execution semantics.
findings.rollback: Remove research ledger instrumentation and fall back to existing runtime logs/Watchtower.

findings.evidence: API-FOOTBALL Pro is limited to 7,500 requests/day and 300/minute (5/sec). Each response reports daily and minute limit/remaining headers. The provider recommends smoothing, caching, avoiding duplicate calls and progressive backoff after 429 responses.
findings.why_it_matters: ARGUS should manage live data from provider truth rather than estimates, preventing false quota halts, bursts, wasted calls and unnecessary subscription upgrades.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Persist quota headers and internal-ledger values on existing provider responses only; add no calls and do not increase polling.
findings.required_evidence: At least 1,000 responses across 3 daily reset boundaries, with reconciled header/internal counters and no increased 429 rate.
findings.failure_condition: Counters cannot be reconciled beyond explainable in-flight concurrency, or logging adds provider calls/latency that changes behavior.
findings.rollback: Remove quota telemetry while retaining current guardrails and polling schedule.

findings.evidence: Reliability diagrams directly compare predicted probabilities with observed frequencies. Proper scores such as Brier and log-loss mix calibration/reliability with resolution and uncertainty, so a lower Brier score alone does not prove better calibration. Calibration must use data independent of model fitting.
findings.why_it_matters: ARGUS is selective. Global calibration can hide overconfidence specifically among PRIME/VALUE decisions, which is the subset operators actually care about.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Without changing thresholds, report reliability bins, Brier, log-loss, calibration error and sample count for ALL, ACCEPTED, PRIME, VALUE and NO_BET cohorts on temporally held-out data.
findings.required_evidence: Start trend reading at >=200 settled accepted selections; prefer >=500 with multiple walk-forward windows and league/market stability before strong conclusions.
findings.failure_condition: Accepted cohorts are materially less reliable than the universe, bins are too sparse, or conclusions reverse across temporal windows.
findings.rollback: Reporting-only; remove cohort report with no decision-state effect.

source: Bai & Jin, Conformal Selective Prediction with General Risk Control, arXiv 2026-03-25
Bao et al., CAP: Calibration after Adaptive Pick, JMLR 2025
findings.evidence: Modern selective-prediction work evaluates risk on the subset a model chooses to trust and highlights post-selection calibration/coverage issues. Online adaptive selection requires special care because selection changes the inferential target.
findings.why_it_matters: ARGUS NO BET should be judged by whether risk actually falls as coverage decreases, not by the intuitive appeal of a confidence threshold.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Generate empirical risk-versus-coverage curves from frozen historical decisions using current readiness/confidence ranking; do not introduce conformal thresholds yet.
findings.required_evidence: Several hundred settled independent matches per broad market, repeated across multiple forward temporal windows; confidence intervals clustered by match where live states repeat.
findings.failure_condition: Risk does not decrease consistently as coverage falls, or apparent gains vanish under forward splits/clustered uncertainty.
findings.rollback: Discard the candidate ranking interpretation; existing NO BET logic stays unchanged.

source: Bai & Jin 2026 selective conformal risk control
Xu, Guo & Wei 2025/2026 Selective Conformal Risk Control
findings.evidence: Recent methods offer finite-sample or PAC-style risk/coverage guarantees under specific assumptions, but the published demonstrations are not football-betting validations and exchangeability/shift assumptions are nontrivial in evolving leagues and markets.
findings.why_it_matters: A formal abstention layer could eventually make ARGUS trust gates more principled, but importing guarantees without verifying assumptions would create false certainty.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Shadow-only retrospective replication after empirical risk/coverage is stable; compare conformal selection with simple confidence quantiles on forward windows.
findings.required_evidence: Stable empirical risk/coverage first, then multiple temporally separated calibration/test windows with explicit shift diagnostics and sufficient independent matches.
findings.failure_condition: Coverage/risk guarantees break materially out-of-time, selection becomes unstable, or simple baselines perform equally well with less complexity.
findings.rollback: Do not integrate conformal thresholds; retain empirical abstention diagnostics only.

findings.source: Clegg, Song & Cartlidge, A market-calibrated accelerated failure time model for in-play football forecasting, arXiv 2026-05-15
findings.evidence: Across 140 EPL matches, calibrating pre-match strength to Betfair 1X2 and over/under prices was reported as the dominant accuracy driver; adding time-varying post-shot xG supported in-play updates. The study is small and league-specific, and its reported betting returns are not independent validation.
findings.why_it_matters: ARGUS should test a simple market-anchored live challenger before investing in a much larger live architecture. The market is a powerful baseline that any claimed edge must beat or complement.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Shadow challenger initialized from frozen, de-vigged kickoff 1X2 + O/U probabilities, updated only by already timestamp-safe live features; compare with market-only and current ARGUS.
findings.required_evidence: >=1,000 independent matches across several leagues and forward windows, evaluated by clustered Brier/log-loss, calibration and additive improvement over market-only.
findings.failure_condition: Gain disappears outside EPL, model only mirrors market, or no reproducible OOS improvement remains after clustering by match.
findings.rollback: Delete challenger outputs; production live logic remains untouched.

findings.evidence: Dixon-Coles modifies low-score probabilities where independent Poisson assumptions are weak. More recent peer-reviewed work across five European leagues argues that standard dependence assumptions are not universally justified and reports gains from richer conditional dependence structures.
findings.why_it_matters: Exact-score probabilities are sensitive to dependence assumptions. ARGUS should benchmark simple independent Poisson, Dixon-Coles and one richer dependence challenger rather than assume a single score model is universally correct.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Replay-only three-model comparison on frozen historical data; score the entire probability matrix, not just the modal exact score.
findings.required_evidence: >=2,000 held-out matches across multiple leagues/seasons and several rolling-origin windows; evaluate full-distribution log-loss, ranked probability/Brier-style scores, calibration and 1X2/O-U coherence.
findings.failure_condition: Richer dependence does not improve OOS probabilistic scores consistently, adds unstable parameters, or violates coherence with derived markets.
findings.rollback: Keep the simplest validated score model; discard challenger parameters/results.

findings.source: Maia et al., Stochastic modelling of football matches using dynamic regressors, International Journal of Forecasting 2026
findings.evidence: Peer-reviewed work models goals and other football events as Cox processes with dynamic regressors and explicitly models stoppage-time lengths, illustrated on eight seasons of Brazilian Serie A data.
findings.why_it_matters: This supports the hypothesis that event timing and stoppage time can matter in live probability updates, but ARGUS should not adopt the framework until event feeds are complete and point-in-time safe.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Do not build the model yet. First audit whether ARGUS has sufficiently complete, timestamped event and stoppage-time data to reproduce a simple hazard baseline.
findings.required_evidence: Documented coverage/latency audit plus a large replay set with event timestamps known to precede each decision state.
findings.failure_condition: Event timestamps are incomplete/late, coverage differs materially by league, or a simpler elapsed-time/score-state baseline performs equally well.
findings.rollback: No model integration; retain as research candidate only.

findings.evidence: Reported ROI from small live-football studies and formal guarantees from non-football selective-prediction settings do not establish deployable ARGUS edge. Different markets, latency, selection, dependence and temporal shift can invalidate direct transfer.
findings.why_it_matters: Copying attractive claims is a direct route to overconfidence and overfitting.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: None in production. Claims may only seed pre-registered shadow replications.
findings.required_evidence: Independent ARGUS-specific multi-window OOS replication with realistic timing, costs, market baseline and sufficient independent matches.
findings.failure_condition: Any proposal relies mainly on published ROI, classification accuracy, or nominal coverage without ARGUS-specific forward validation.

watch: Formal conformal/selective thresholds only after empirical risk-coverage stability is demonstrated.
Dynamic event-process live modelling only after timestamp/coverage audit proves event data is point-in-time safe.
do_not_do: Do not increase PRIME confidence or loosen NO BET from this research dossier.
Do not treat Brier/log-loss alone as proof of calibration; inspect reliability directly.
Do not increase API polling or upgrade API-Football to hide quota/control defects.
Do not treat configured cron state as proof of successful persisted execution.
Do not auto-fix the widespread url.parse() warning until its dependency/origin is identified and a replacement is regression-tested.
Do not copy reported live ROI or formal conformal guarantees without ARGUS-specific OOS replication.
Do not add a complex exact-score or live model before simple baselines are beaten consistently.
Do not modify production from this dossier.
